evidence.note: Opens with the proposition: a shared rooftop array could undercut daytime power costs for blocks C and D; subtitle proposes a 12-month pilot on two roofs.
Problem made concrete: about 40% of flats' electricity spend falls in daylight hours, with a £612 median yearly spend per flat as the hero stat.

Labelled Problem but the title is resident support (26 of 33 support a pilot); the resident quote about paying peak rates under the roof carries the felt stakes. The saving per flat is never stated as a figure.
Resolution: a 12-month pilot (64 kW, £86,400) running Install → 12 months measured → Go or stop review.
Mechanism builds step by step: shared array → landlord supply → flats' monthly credit, ending on the insight that heavy daytime users get the largest credit.
Risks and the disputed payback (7 vs 11 years) are laid out before the ask.
Closes with a clear ask: the board approves the £86,400 pilot with a go or stop review at twelve months.

rationale: The deck moves clearly from problem (daylight share of a £612 bill) through resident stakes and support to a pilot resolution, risks and a specific board ask that follows from the pilot slides. The weak link is the stakes step: s-3 swaps from cost to survey support, and the deck never turns the 40% daylight share into a concrete saving per flat. That fits level 4: a clear arc ending in an ask, with one weak transition.
